title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
description: Choose ten distinct study environments. Verify access rules, room or reservation constraints, and the physical affordance that makes each useful. Treat “Claimed by 9am” as editorial framing; never assert crowding or student behavior without evidence.

cards.entity_name: Charles Chu Asian Art Reading Room
cards.title: Charles Chu Asian Art Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Shain Library, First Floor
cards.notes: Study in a serene environment surrounded by Chinese scrolls and Asian art. This quiet reading area features comfortable armchairs and large windows for natural light.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, art-filled reading room on the main floor of Shain Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Charles Chu Asian Art Reading Room serves as both a quiet reading area and a permanent exhibition space for Asian art.
cards.source_title: Charles Chu Asian Art Reading Room - Connecticut College
cards.access_notes: Open during Shain Library hours; typically accessible to students for quiet study.

cards.title: Blue Camel Café
cards.subtitle: Shain Library, First Floor
cards.notes: Utilize this 24-hour study space for late-night sessions. The cafe offers specialty coffees and snacks in a social atmosphere with both indoor and outdoor seating.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour study space and coffee shop located within Shain Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Blue Camel Café is located in a prominent first-floor spot and doubles as a 24-hour study space.
cards.source_title: Charles E. Shain Library - Connecticut College
cards.access_notes: The cafe space is available for 24-hour study for students with campus access.

cards.title: Shain Library Collaboration Rooms
cards.subtitle: Shain Library, Multiple Floors
cards.notes: Reserve one of ten group rooms equipped with whiteboard walls and LCD panels. These spaces are ideal for team projects and can be booked online via LibCal.
cards.short_summary: Ten reservable group study rooms with digital displays and whiteboards.
cards.evidence_claim: Ten reservable collaboration rooms, each outfitted with whiteboard walls and LCD panels on which students can share laptop displays.
cards.source_title: Charles E. Shain Library - Connecticut College
cards.access_notes: Reservations are required through the library's online booking system.

cards.title: Greer Music Library
cards.subtitle: Cummings Arts Center, Lower Level
cards.notes: Find a quiet nook or reading table among 20,000 recordings and scores. This specialized library offers a traditional atmosphere for focused academic work.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, specialized library for music research and study in Cummings Arts Center.
cards.evidence_claim: A comfortable reading area, tables and nooks provide library users with a variety of spaces for both quiet and collaborative study.
cards.access_notes: Open during posted music library hours; accessible to all students.

cards.title: Blaustein Humanities Center Third Floor
cards.subtitle: Blaustein Humanities Center
cards.notes: Study at the large tables or lounge chairs in the wings of the third floor. This area is known for its calm atmosphere and proximity to campus coffee shops.
cards.short_summary: A quiet study area with tables and couches on the top floor of Blaustein.
cards.evidence_claim: Blaustein is a criminally underrated place to get work done... the cozy tables in the third floor wings.
cards.source_title: New Camels, Find Your On-Campus Oasis! | The College Voice
cards.access_notes: Accessible during building hours; typically quietest during non-class times.

cards.title: New London Hall Classrooms
cards.subtitle: New London Hall
cards.notes: Gather for group study in these modern life sciences classrooms. The building features large windows with campus views and state-of-the-art facilities.
cards.short_summary: Modern classrooms in the life sciences building used for group study.
cards.evidence_claim: One of the best places to study as a group on campus is New London Hall... we have taken one of the classrooms and worked at the desks together.
cards.source_title: Our Favorite Study Spots On Campus - Her Campus
cards.access_notes: Available for study when classes are not in session; building access required.

cards.title: Tempel Green Outdoor Classroom
cards.subtitle: Tempel Green
cards.notes: Study outdoors at the granite-fashioned classroom on the green. This spot offers views of Long Island Sound and is popular for group sessions in warmer months.
cards.short_summary: A granite outdoor classroom located on the main campus green.
cards.evidence_claim: Some professors move their classes to Tempel Green, which features an outdoor classroom fashioned from granite.
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7; best used during daylight hours in fair weather.

cards.title: Zachs Hillel House Great Room
cards.subtitle: Zachs Hillel House
cards.notes: Work in the Great Room, which is designed for studying, lectures, and dinners. The house also features a library and comfortable lounge seating for students.
cards.short_summary: A multi-purpose study and community space within the Zachs Hillel House.
cards.evidence_claim: The building features a kosher kitchen; a great room for studying, lectures and dinners; a library; conference room; and office space.
cards.access_notes: Accessible to the campus community; check for scheduled events.

cards.title: Crozier-Williams Student Lounge
cards.subtitle: College Center at Crozier-Williams
cards.notes: Find a spot in the heart of campus activity at 'Cro.' The center offers various lounge areas and collaborative spaces near student organization offices.
cards.short_summary: Central campus center lounge areas for social and informal study.
cards.evidence_claim: A renovated Cro... can fully realize its potential as a space that brings faculty, staff and students together for formal, informal and coincidental interactions.
cards.access_notes: Open during building hours; typically high-traffic and social.

cards.title: Technology Commons
cards.subtitle: Shain Library, Lower Level
cards.notes: Access high-performance workstations and the Visualization Wall. This lower-level space is designed for digital projects and collaborative tech-heavy work.
cards.short_summary: A tech-focused collaborative study space on the lower level of Shain Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Lower-level spaces include the Technology Commons, providing an array of seating for group work; an Advanced Workstation Cluster... and the Visualization Wall.
cards.source_title: Charles E. Shain Library - Connecticut College
cards.access_notes: Open during Shain Library hours; specialized software available on workstations.
